[📖]{.ref-verdict .note} [The definitions this course uses: reproducibility (same data, same code) vs replicability (new data, same question).]{.ref-msg}

:::: {.ref-item}
[✓]{.ref-verdict .good} [Doing it right: a one-page card stating what a model is for and where it breaks — now expected on every model hub.]{.ref-msg}

[Mitchell, M., et al. (2019). Model cards for model reporting. *Proceedings of FAT\* '19*, 220–229.]{.ref-cite}

:::: {.ref-item}
[✓]{.ref-verdict .good} [A whole conference made reproducibility a submission checklist — and measured what changed.]{.ref-msg}

[Pineau, J., et al. (2021). Improving reproducibility in machine learning research. *Journal of Machine Learning Research*, 22(164), 1–20.]{.ref-cite}

:::: {.ref-item}
[✗]{.ref-verdict .bad} [Retracted within a year: an ocean-warming headline whose systematic errors were treated as random — caught by an outside reader, not the workflow.]{.ref-msg}

[Resplandy, L., et al. (2018). Quantification of ocean heat uptake from changes in atmospheric O₂ and CO₂ composition. *Nature*, 563, 105–108. Retracted 2019 (Retraction Note: *Nature*, 573, 614) after the reported uncertainties proved underestimated.]{.ref-cite}
